Subject: Retention extractability & compressed log policy — evidence request

Hi Ben,

Thanks for taking this. Were working through a CAIQ/SIG review and have a couple of specific asks around your log retention and deletion controls before we close the questionnaire:

1) Compressed/packed logs: weve heard that some providers store tenant logs as compressed blobs or parquet chunks to save cost. If Redwood uses compressed storage for tenant/session logs, can you confirm whether those blobs are still "exportable" in a readable format for a customer or third-party forensics? If yes, what is the typical turnaround time and format?

2) Proof of delete: For short retention carveouts (customer-controlled override to 30 days vs default 90), our legal team requires evidence of deletion that shows the file-level deletion job and eventual object lifecycle removal. What canonical artifacts do you deliver (deletion job logs, object version manifests, S3 lifecycle timestamp, signed attestations)?

3) Sampling / aggregations: For customers that request minimized retention (e.g., only summaries/aggregates, no raw request bodies), how do you track that filtered retention was applied correctly? Do you provide an artifacts package that ties a retention policy change to exported samples and the prior retention window?

If possible, wed like a short evidence pack suitable for SOC 2/CAIQ review and any guidance on the process for requesting a customer-specific exception. Our timeline is tightwed prefer something this week.

Thanks,
Alex Mercer
Security Engineer, Cobalt Therapeutics
security@cobalttx.com

Alex,

Appreciate the clear asks. Short answers up front:
- Compressed logs: yes, we store some inference trace and debug logs in compressed columnar blobs by default for cold retention tiers, but we can export them in readable JSON/CSV if needed. Typical turnaround is 24-72 hours depending on dataset size.
- Proof-of-delete: our standard evidence bundle includes the deletion job run log, the object manifest with tombstone/version ids, and a signed "proof of erase" note from our operations team. We can also provide a CSV manifest that maps original tenant IDs to removed object keys for forensic review.
- Sampling/minimized retention: we produce a retention_matrix entry and a sample export that demonstrates the filtering rules were applied; the sample is hashed and cross-referenced against the original manifest so you can validate.

Im looping in Stephanie (Security/compliance) and Priyom (Product/ops) to pull the canonical artifact pack we use for CAIQ/SIG requests and to confirm any timing constraints.

I can send an evidence pack and a short runbook for requesting a 30-day carveout today, but if you need formal signed attestations well need formal acceptance of the exception via our Security Exception request form (link below) and that usually takes a day to process.

Links to what Ill attach: SOC 2 report (redacted), retention matrix (Cobalt subset), proof_of_delete template. If you want the raw manifests instead of hashed manifests we can do that under an NDA; otherwise we deliver hashed manifests for privacy by default.

Ben

Alex,

Thanks for the patiencewe pulled the artifacts together and attached a compact evidence pack. Quick summary of whats attached and how it maps to your asks: 

1) redwood_soc2_report_2027.pdf (attached) — SOC 2 Type II report (redacted). Section 6.2 and Appendix B describe our data lifecycle controls and object lifecycle deletion procedures.

2) retention_matrix_cobalt_subset.csv (attached) — a cut of our retention matrix showing the Cobalt tenant policy (30-day carveout requested) and the storage tier mapping (hot/warm/cold). Notes column documents whether data is stored compressed and the canonical export format.

3) proof_of_delete_template.txt (attached) — this is the artifact we deliver for deletion events: it includes deletion job id, run timestamps, object key manifest (hashed by default), S3 version/tombstone ids, and a signed operations attestation. If you need raw keys for forensics we can do that under your NDA; please confirm and we will initiate an exception request.

Process & timings:
- Exports of compressed blobs are done via our export worker that materializes the blobs into newline-delimited JSON or CSV. For the Cobalt subset we estimate 24 hours for the sample size you described; large full-volume exports can take up to 72 hours.
- Proof-of-delete delivery: when a deletion job runs we generate the proof_of_delete artifact and can post it securely to a customer SFTP or encrypted Drive link. The standard SLA for artifact delivery is 24 hours post-job completion.

Next steps if you want raw manifests: sign the NDA (we can reuse your existing inter-company NDA if available), confirm the scope (tenant IDs/time window), and Ill kick off a security-exception form so Priyom and Ops can schedule the export. Ive included the drive link to the evidence pack above and a HubSpot ticket for tracking.

If youd like a short Zoom to walk through the artifacts and the manifest format, I can set that up for tomorrow morning.

Ben
